headline: Approved February 2026 minutes and reviewed progress on accessibility projects including the Lions Club library collaboration and MOD grant installation.
summary: The Disability Commission approved its February 2026 meeting minutes by unanimous roll call vote. Members gave updates on the Lions Club library accessibility project, the MOD grant-funded installation at the High School, and the Vision 2026 TIESHERRA framework covering transportation, education, social activities, employment, housing, and policy research. No new business was raised and no one spoke during public comment.
decisions: Approved the February 2026 meeting minutes, unanimous by roll call vote.

Disability Commission Meeting Minutes 
March 12, 2026 
Attendance: 
 
 
This meeting included remote participation. Some members of the Disability Commission 
participated in the meeting remotely per the Governor’s legislation of March 28, 2025, 
suspending certain provisions of the open meeting law. A Microsoft Teams link was also 
provided for members of the public who wished to attend remotely. 
 
This meeting was also recorded through Microsoft Teams and called to order at 6:04PM. 
 
1.  Roll call of Committee Members 
Chuks started the meeting and mentioned that it would be recorded via Microsoft 
Teams. He then called attendance as indicated in the chart above and a quorum was 
present to conduct business. Each member gave a self-description when responding 
to roll call.   
 
2. Approval of Meeting Minutes 
The February 2026 minutes were discussed. Upon motion of Ralph to approve the 
February minutes, seconded by Lisa, the Commission voted unanimously by roll call 
vote to approve the minutes.     
 
3. Updates or Action Items that need to be Addressed from Previous Meetings 
 
• Lions Club Collaboration: Chuks reported that the aim of the project is to 
enhance accessibility at the Malden Public Library, including ongoing coordination 
with the library director and Malden Lions Club representatives. Chuks and Kate 
D. attended a meeting with the Lions Club and are now working to schedule a 
follow-up meeting with the library director. In terms of possible equipment, the 
Lions Club is oﬀering to make a donation towards the expense. Michelle Luong is 
the contact person.

• MOD Grant: Maria reported on the progress of the grant-funded project at the 
High School. Eric Rubin has purchased the accessible sinks and other items 
needed for the installation and they should arrive over the next week. The goal is 
to complete the installation within the next month. The Commission discussed 
strategies for publicizing these improvements and Marilyn suggested the use of 
press releases and Parent Square used by the schools for broader community 
awareness. Maria will connect with the Superintendent.  
Chucks mentioned other potential grants and referenced the most recent MOD 
newsletter announcing their funding opportunities. Maria agreed to investigate 
this as a potential supplement to the Lions Club's eﬀorts. The Commission had 
discussed a library project during the last grant cycle but there had not been 
enough time to obtain estimates. 
• Vision 2026: Chuks reminded the Commission of the T I E S H E R R A Framework 
that will be used to organize efforts across Transportation, Infrastructure, 
Education, Social Activities, Health, Employment, Recreation, Religion, 
Rehabilitation, and Accommodation. The goal is to make an impact in each of 
these sectors. Members reported on their assigned areas of interest. 
Transportation and Infrastructure: Lisa reported that she will keep a 
spreadsheet tracking accessible transportation options and infrastructure 
issues, such as dangerous sidewalks and potholes. She also discussed the need 
for community input via surveys or online reporting. Maria suggested sending 
a list of the problematic intersections and infrastructure issues to forward to 
the city engineer.  
 
Education Initiatives: Marilyn summarized activities of the Malden SEPAC, the 
Bright Minds Quiet Spaces event, the Malden Behavioral Health Center 
outreach, and an upcoming DESE seminar. She emphasized partnerships and 
advocacy. Marilyn will prepare a one- to two-page written report on 
education initiatives for the next meeting to serve as a source for the 
Commission. 
 
Social Activities and Health: Kate D. reported on the planning of the bird 
watching event. She discussed the need for coordination with the DPW 
regarding the signage because it was removed prior to the event last year. 
Kate D. also mentioned the need for accessible facilities, looking into food 
licensing, as well as ongoing outreach to health organizations. She will keep 
the Commission updated. 
Employment Activities: Maria reported on a possible collaboration with 
Project Triangle and Mass Ability, both local agencies providing vocational 
training and employment support for individuals with disabilities. She is 
hoping to invite agency representatives to future meetings. 
Housing and Accommodations: Chuks reported that he is the liaison for the 
Commission with the Human Rights and Fair Housing Commission. They are
3 | Page  
 
working to address disability-related housing issues, emphasizing advocacy for 
ADA compliance and human rights.  
Kate H. expressed an interest in the areas of Policy Research and Advocacy. 
She proposed and discussed the idea of focusing on policy research, 
monitoring relevant legislation and regulations at federal, state, and local 
levels. This would help the Commission stay informed and responsive.  
5.   New Business 
 No further business discussed. 
 
6. Public Comment 
No one spoke for public comment.  
 
7.   Scheduling of next meeting and adjournment 
The next meeting was scheduled for Thursday, April 9, 2026 at 6:00PM. Upon the 
motion of Maria to adjourn, which was seconded by Kate H., the Commission voted 
unanimously to adjourn the meeting.
